The Respondents are duly served with the notice.
Respondent No.2 is absent, hence, proceed ex-parte against Respondent No.2.

2. Heard learned Counsel for the Appellant and Respondent No.1/Original Claimant.
3.

This Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 against the Judgment and Award dated 13 th October 2022 passed in MACP No. 205 of 2015, whereby the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.8,82,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of registration of the Claim Petition till realisation of the amount.
4. It is the contention of the Appellant/Insurer that the Tribunal committed error in granting compensation of Rs. 8,82,000/- when the amount of compensation was sought of Rs. 4 lakhs.
It is submitted that there is no justification for enhancement of such compensation by the Tribunal.
Secondly, it is contended that there is a serious dispute with regard to the coverage of the offending vehicle at the relevant time under Insurance Policy.
5th January 2026 6-fa208-2023-OJ.doc 5.

The learned counsel for the Appellant submits that the Insurer had raised the issue with regard to the non-coverage of the offending vehicle by the valid Insurance Policy during the relevant time by filing Written Statement and other contentions of the Claimant were also denied by the Insurer.

It is his submission that the Tribunal has failed to take into consideration the evidence on record which,
according to him, indicates that though the cover note was issued on 26th February 2014, the Insurance Policy was not issued on the same date.
On the point of quantum, it is the submission that the Tribunal has granted excess compensation, which was not claimed by the Claimant.
6. Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1/Original Claimant supported the impugned Judgment and Award.
He drew attention of the Court to the cover note indicating date of its insurance on 26th February, 2014, so also, the policy being issued on 26th February 2014 itself.

In respect of compensation granted by the Tribunal, he placed reliance on the Judgment in the case of Nagappa vs Gurudayal Singh & Ors1 to submit that it is open for the Tribunal to grant just compensation,
even if it is not so prayed.

There cannot be any dispute made with regard to the prepositions sought to be canvassed by the learned counsel for the Claimant that, it is open for the Tribunal to grant just and reasonable amount of compensation, if not claimed, in view of judgment in case of Nagappa (supra).
Thus, this Court finds no substance in the challenge to the impugned Judgment and Award on this count.

8. Insofar as the defence of non-coverage of the offending vehicle in the accident is concerned,
though a plea is raised by the Insurer to that effect, there is no evidence to substantiate the same.

sentences.text: the other hand, the material evidence brought on record indicates that the cover note was issued on 26th February 2014 so also, the policy was issued on the same day.
The accident has admittedly occurred on 27th February 2014.
The evidence on record unerringly shows that the offending vehicle was duly ensured with the Appellant on the date of accident.
9. In such circumstances, this Court finds no substance in the challenge to the impugned Judgment and Award on this Count too.
5th January 2026 6-fa208-2023-OJ.doc 10.
As a result of above discussion, there is no merit in the Appeal.

11. In view of the above, I pass the following order:
ORDER (a) The Appeal is dismissed.
(b) The Claimants are permitted to withdraw the deposited amount along with accrued interest thereon.
(c) The statutory amount be transmitted to the Tribunal along with accrued interest thereon.
The parties are at liberty to withdraw it as per Rule.
(d) R & P be sent back to the Tribunal.
12. In view of dismissal of the Appeals, pending Applications, if any, stand disposed of.
